kind: Retrospective finding-origin assessment from actual repair reviews

original_contract.scope: Repair structured-report verifier so a kill requires the intended test/stage/error/assertion identity; preserve valid alternatives and distinguish unrun checks. Malformed return-code validation was not specified by the stated fixture contract.

findings.evidence: The acceptance review found hardcoded-stage/test/assertion classifiers pass instrument revision4 even though the original identity contract required reading these fields from the report target.
findings.disposition: Repair in scope; revision5 adds transfer assertions and negative controls. Saved native classifier passes offline; hardcoded alternatives fail.

findings.evidence: Adding the native revision4 attempt extended the record to ten samples with a 600-second sample; aggregate prose still said nine samples and 240 seconds. Those statements became inaccurate when the new attempt was added.
findings.disposition: Correct counts/budget at 2c21841 without changing old attempts.

findings.evidence: The saved classifier accepts matching identity with malformed return codes such as null or a string. The recorded fixture supplied ordinary numeric return codes; the contract did not specify malformed-input validation.
findings.disposition: Disclose and defer malformed-input hardening rather than expanding this bounded verifier repair. This is not a claim malformed inputs are safe in a production verifier.
